document.recommended_title: When Online Guarantees Go Silent: Feasibility and Evasion in ML Intrusion Detection
document.alternative_title: Validity Is Not Viability: Feasibility and Attackability of Online Error Control for ML Intrusion Detection

submission_constraints.editorial_implication: Every central theorem statement, proof idea, primary empirical result, and essential limitation must remain in the body. Appendices should verify and broaden the story, not carry it.

central_thesis: A statistical error-control layer can be formally valid yet operationally empty at security-scale horizons; the aggregation used to recover feasibility then becomes an adversarial attack surface.

paper_identity.what_it_is: A compositional security analysis of a statistical trust layer for ML intrusion detection.
what_it_is_not: A broad benchmark of every online testing method
A general claim that online FDR is unusable
A general claim that every host-aware detector is padding-vulnerable
two_principal_contributions: C1: finite discovery horizon and exact calibration-horizon boundary
C2: aggregation and adaptive state as attack surfaces
paper_identity.bridge_not_third_contribution: Grouping reduces the hypothesis horizon and buys feasibility exactly, but loses semantic resolution and creates the composition attacked by C2.

strongest_contributions.name: Finite discovery horizon and exact feasibility boundary
strongest_contributions.one_sentence_pitch: For two controller families containing LOND, e-LOND, e-LORD, and LORD++, bounded conformal evidence and uninterrupted summable spending produce a finite, absorbing rejection horizon.
must_keep_in_body: 20 calibration units per hypothesis for e-LOND at k=1 and alpha=0.05
decisive_evidence: Approximately 3.3e8 calibration flows required for LOND/e-LOND at flow-scale LSPR23 horizon
Approximately 6.5e8 for LORD++
Approximately 3.2e13 under gamma_j proportional to j^-1.6
Only 1.8e6 to 2.4e6 calibration flows available
Only the first 748 to 902 grouped hypotheses are cold-start feasible under the horizon-free sequence
strongest_contributions.novelty_positioning: Prior work observed conformal resolution loss or alpha-death. The manuscript adds structural conditions, a finite absorbing horizon, an exact count-ratio boundary, and a classification of escape mechanisms and their costs.

strongest_contributions.name: Symmetric e-merging is inherently vulnerable to zero-evidence padding
strongest_contributions.one_sentence_pitch: No symmetric e-merging family that can cross a rejection threshold above one can be invariant to appending zero-evidence members.
must_keep_in_body: Black-box construction versus oracle-minimal sizing distinction
decisive_evidence: Primary canonical detections cost 23, 24, and 33 added flows
Replication canonical median cost is 6 flows over 11 detections
Controlled replay suppresses 3/3 and 34/34 canonical targets at the predicted threshold
AIT flow-only chain suppresses 84/85 true detections across eight organizations
AIT host-conditioned end-to-end replay suppresses 9/9 evaluated detections
critical_scope: Constructing plausible padding is black-box; exact minimum sizing is an oracle lower bound
Transfer covers the implemented six host-context features and accumulation model, not all host-aware detectors
The theorem applies to symmetric e-merging families that attain the threshold

strongest_contributions.name: Granularity-feasibility-resolution bridge
strongest_contributions.one_sentence_pitch: Coarsening the hypothesis reduces T and buys feasibility in exact lockstep, while each alert represents more fine-grained attack activity.
must_keep_in_body: Exact linear dependence on grouped-hypothesis count
Alert blur as the preferred cost metric
Causal handoff from C1 to C2
decisive_evidence: Primary-window blur rises from 1.0 at five minutes to 16.1 at two hours and 38.5 at one day
Stress-window blur rises from 1.0 to 20.4
Source-host grouping is feasible at every tested bucket, showing that the barrier can be bought off
do_not_use_as_headline_metric: Malicious-flow coverage dominated by a few high-mass episodes

strongest_contributions.name: Evidence-conditioned controller state can be attacker-controlled
strongest_contributions.one_sentence_pitch: ADDIS escapes absorption by conditioning its spending index on observed evidence, and attacker-generated selected non-candidates can advance that index until all later targets are silent.
must_keep_in_body: Real stress-window mechanism demonstration clearly marked invalid for guarantees
decisive_evidence: Real stress window has sharp transition at B*=203 precursors
Each precursor requires 453279 flows in that configuration
Total real-stream budget is 92015637 flows, 36.1 GB, and 33.4 Mbit/s
Synthetic valid streams have median B*=140, range 140 to 255, and all 120 targets are silenced
Synthetic mixed-stream mean FDP is 0.047 at q=0.05
critical_scope: The real-stream evidence is invalid and supports mechanism/cost only
The attack is conspicuous, not low footprint
The attack does not cover online e-BH's history-wide fixed point

strongest_contributions.name: Group-validity premise and cost of direct group calibration
strongest_contributions.role: Credibility and dependency result, not headline contribution
strongest_contributions.one_sentence_pitch: The grouped e-value guarantee needs a local metadata-conditional premise; calibrating groups directly removes that premise but collapses the evidence ceiling and stops primary/replication alerting.
decisive_evidence: Position 0.85 benign firing rate is 50.9 times nominal and gives E[e] approximately 51
Other windows have only 0 to 3 benign firings and cannot validate the premise
Direct group calibration reduces calibration units to 37k to 57k, makes margin about -0.97, and yields zero primary/replication detections

story_arc.heading: A guarantee is only useful if any evidence can cross its threshold
story_arc.logic: Finite calibration creates a hard evidence ceiling; online spending creates a shrinking threshold.

story_arc.heading: The collision creates a finite discovery horizon
story_arc.logic: For the covered families, a rejection-free run eventually enters an absorbing infeasible state.

story_arc.heading: The defender must reduce the number of hypotheses or change the temporal guarantee
story_arc.logic: Grouping, restart, smoothing, or deferred decisions remove or relax different premises and have distinct prices.

story_arc.heading: Grouping is the direct operational repair
story_arc.logic: Reducing T lowers the calibration requirement exactly but coarsens the semantic unit.

story_arc.heading: The repair becomes the attack surface
story_arc.logic: Attacker-controlled group membership permits zero-evidence padding; symmetric valid aggregation cannot make that impossible.

story_arc.heading: Adaptive escape mechanisms can expose state as well
story_arc.logic: When evidence determines the spending index, attacker-generated evidence can control future levels.

story_arc.heading: Therefore evaluate the composed trust layer
story_arc.logic: Validity, feasibility, semantic granularity, and adversarial robustness are separate system properties.

reviewer_risks.risk: Novelty objection: finite conformal resolution and alpha-death are already known
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: State the novelty delta in the introduction and related work: absorbing structural horizon, exact exchange rate, procedure-family conditions, and escape classification/cost.

reviewer_risks.risk: Reviewers may think the empirical FDR guarantee was validated on LSPR23
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: Use one scope/dependency table and state that Assumption 1 is not established; four windows are merely not refuted and 0.85 is invalid.

reviewer_risks.risk: The paper appears to be a collection of unrelated experiments
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: Enforce one causal chain: bounded evidence -> finite horizon -> grouping -> resolution cost -> padding -> adaptive state.

reviewer_risks.risk: ADDIS state attack is over-sold despite invalid real evidence and high cost
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: Make it a short supporting result, foreground the synthetic-valid mechanism, call the real cost conspicuous, and exclude online e-BH.

reviewer_risks.risk: Padding is called black-box although exact costs use live state
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: Separate black-box construction from oracle-minimum sizing in the threat model, theorem discussion, table footnote, and limitations.

reviewer_risks.risk: Dual reporting under canonical and first-flow orders overwhelms the story
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: Use canonical order in the main body. Keep first-flow only as an appendix robustness/optimistic-detection bound.

reviewer_risks.risk: The transfer result is interpreted as a universal failure of host-aware detection
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: State exact tested features, causal replay, organizations, and uncovered regimes.

reviewer_risks.risk: Critical results live only in unlimited appendices
reviewer_risks.response_in_rewrite: Keep all central theorem statements, proof ideas, primary/replication evidence, and limitation scopes in the 12-page body.

final_compression_checks: The abstract contains one C1 result, the bridge, one Surface A result, and one short Surface B sentence.
The introduction names exactly two principal contributions and one bridge.
Primary and replication evidence dominate the empirical narrative.
The invalid stress result is visually and verbally marked as mechanism/cost only.
Canonical order is the only main-body ordering; first-flow matrices are appendix material.
No main caption repeats the threat model, order convention, and validity caveat.
Every central theorem has its condition, conclusion, and proof idea in the body.
Every guarantee-bearing empirical claim is conditional on Assumption 1.
The paper never treats failure to reject a validity diagnostic as positive evidence.
The state attack is described as conspicuous, not low cost.
The padding construction is black-box and the exact minimum is oracle-sized.
The final paragraph returns to composed-system evaluation rather than experiment count.
